concepts.title: Slope of a Line from Two Points
concepts.definition: The slope measures the tilt of a line as the tangent of its inclination; between two known points it equals the vertical change divided by the horizontal change, and vertical lines carry no defined slope.
concepts.key_idea: Rise over run; equal slopes mean parallel lines.

concepts.title: Perpendicular Slopes and Negative Reciprocal
concepts.definition: Two non-vertical lines stand perpendicular exactly when the product of their slopes is minus one; the slope of a perpendicular is therefore the negative reciprocal, and for a general line the slope is minus the x coefficient over the y coefficient.
concepts.key_idea: Flip the slope and flip its sign; parallel keeps it unchanged.

concepts.title: Forms of the Equation of a Line
concepts.definition: A straight line can be written from limited data: a point with a slope gives the point-slope form, a slope with the axis crossing gives the slope-intercept form, two axis crossings give the intercept form, and any line arranges into the general form with x and y coefficients.
concepts.key_idea: Recover the intercept from one point and the slope; then evaluate anywhere.

concepts.title: Intersection of Two Lines and Market Equilibrium
concepts.definition: Two non-parallel lines meet where their expressions agree; equating them and solving gives the meeting point, which for supply and demand curves pins down the equilibrium price and the equilibrium quantity.
concepts.key_idea: Set the two expressions equal, solve for the shared variable, back-substitute for the other.

concepts.title: Distance of a Point from a Line
concepts.definition: The shortest reach from a point to a line runs perpendicular to it; substituting the point into the line expression and dividing by the square root of the squared coefficients gives that perpendicular length.
concepts.formula: d = abs(a * x1 + b * y1 + c) / sqrt(a**2 + b**2)
concepts.key_idea: Evaluate the line at the point, then normalise by the coefficient magnitude.

concepts.title: Distance Between Parallel Lines
concepts.definition: Two parallel lines share their x and y coefficients and differ only in the constant; their separation equals the gap between the constants divided by the magnitude of the shared coefficient pair.
concepts.key_idea: Same coefficients means one subtraction and one normalisation.

concepts.title: Equation, Centre and Radius of a Circle
concepts.definition: A circle collects points at one fixed distance from a centre; its central form squares the coordinate offsets, and a general quadratic without an xy term and with equal x and y coefficients hides a centre at the negated half coefficients with a radius from the constant.
concepts.key_idea: Centre at minus half the linear coefficients; radius squares the halves minus the constant.

concepts.title: Parabola Parameter, Focus and Latus Rectum
concepts.definition: A parabola collects points equidistant from a focus and a directrix; the opening width parameter a follows from any known point on the curve, the focus sits at distance a along the axis, and the focal chord across the axis measures four times a.
concepts.key_idea: Feed one curve point into the standard equation; the focus and focal chord follow from a.
